Update: I pushed another leak-focused patchset and validated it against the MCP fanout repro.

Commits (in my fork `dzianisv/opencode`, branch `dev`):
- `7c7fc91d4` — lazy-load MCP clients for status/bootstrap paths
- `89ecf7b67` — dynamic MCP command refresh + lazy-connect regression tests
- `84a1a0aaa` — make MCP tool runtime opt-in (no implicit auto-connect for configured MCPs unless connected/enabled)
- `bb3b2e143` — docs update for MCP memory probe + opt-in behavior

What changed in behavior:
- `GET /mcp` and `GET /command` no longer spawn MCP subprocess trees.
- MCP tool runtime is now opt-in:
  - explicit `POST /mcp/:name/connect` (UI toggle path), or
  - config `mcp.<name>.enabled: true`.
- This prevents background sessions from implicitly starting heavy MCP processes (playwriter/chrome-devtools/whisper/etc.).

Validation summary:
- MCP test suite passes (13 tests).
- typecheck passes.
- process-tree repro check (calling `/mcp` and `/command` across multiple directories):
  - process count stayed flat (`2 -> 2`)
  - no MCP child fanout.

I’m continuing investigation on any remaining non-MCP growth paths, but this removes a major multi-GB process-tree contributor that was reproducible in this issue thread.

Direct commit links:
- https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/7c7fc91d4
- https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/89ecf7b67
- https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/84a1a0aaa
- https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/bb3b2e143

Additional validation after latest commit (`84a1a0aaa`):

Repro flow:
1. Start `opencode serve`
2. Call `GET /mcp`, `GET /command`, create session, post a `noReply` message
3. Sample `GET /global/memory?children=true`
4. Explicitly connect `playwriter`, sample again
5. Disconnect `playwriter`, sample again

Observed:
- Before: `count=2`, `tree≈399 MB`
- After `/mcp` + `/command` + session/message churn: `count=2`, `tree≈418 MB` (no MCP fanout)
- After explicit `POST /mcp/playwriter/connect`: `count=4`, `tree≈881 MB` (expected MCP child processes)
- After `POST /mcp/playwriter/disconnect`: `count=2`, `tree≈421 MB`

So the patch is now clearly separating:
- normal UI/session traffic (no implicit MCP subprocess growth)
- explicit MCP enablement (expected memory increase while connected)

One more memory-pressure reduction commit pushed:
- https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/324d93459

Change:
- In `Session.updatePart`, replaced deep `structuredClone(part)` in `message.part.updated` bus publish with a shallow object copy.

Why:
- `updatePart` is high-frequency during streaming/tool execution.
- Deep cloning full part payloads creates large short-lived allocations and GC churn under heavy sessions.

Validation:
- targeted suites pass (`session`, `acp`, `mcp`) and package typecheck passes.

> [@h4rvey-g](https://github.com/h4rvey-g) I was encountering this too on 1.2.26. but then I realized, one of my plugins werwase not using the new PartID format. try troubleshooting your enabled plugins to figure out which one is causing the error.

Thank you! You're right. In my case it's [opencode-supermemory](https://github.com/supermemoryai/opencode-supermemory)

Another leak-path hardening commit pushed:
- https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/c055e6baa

Change:
- `FileTime` now uses bounded maps instead of unbounded nested objects.
- Added caps with env overrides:
  - `OPENCODE_FILETIME_SESSION_MAX` (default `256`)
  - `OPENCODE_FILETIME_FILE_MAX` (default `1024`)
- Oldest entries are evicted LRU-style for both per-session file reads and total session tracking.

Why:
- Prevent unbounded growth of read-timestamp metadata during long-running sessions with heavy file churn.

Validation:
- added eviction tests in `test/file/time.test.ts`
- targeted suites pass (`file/time`, `session`, `acp`, `mcp`)
- package typecheck passes.

Another focused fix landed for high-output shell workloads:

Commits:
- https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/e3fdd9a50
- https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/476d693f1

What changed:
- `SessionPrompt.shell` now:
  - caps in-memory stdout/stderr capture (`OPENCODE_SHELL_CAPTURE_MAX_BYTES`, default 2MB)
  - throttles incremental `message.part.updated` metadata emissions
  - truncates persisted final output via existing `Truncate.output(...)`
- `BashTool` now:
  - caps in-memory capture (`OPENCODE_BASH_CAPTURE_MAX_BYTES`, default 2MB)
  - throttles metadata updates
  - surfaces `clipped` metadata flag

Validation:
- targeted tests pass (tool/bash + session/acp/mcp + file/time suites)
- typecheck passes
- stress repro (`POST /session/:id/shell` with ~8MB output command, 12 times):
  - before this patch: process RSS grew to ~1915MB
  - after this patch: process RSS stayed around ~493MB
  - process count stayed flat (`2`) in both cases

This removes another major memory pressure source during shell-heavy sessions.

Consolidated update: applied fixes + practical memory mitigations

### Fixes already implemented (with commits)

1. Lazy MCP bootstrapping for status/bootstrap paths (avoid process fanout)
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/7c7fc91d4

2. Dynamic MCP command refresh + lazy-connect coverage tests
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/89ecf7b67

3. MCP tool runtime opt-in (no implicit auto-connect fanout)
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/84a1a0aaa

4. Replace deep clone churn on part update publish path
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/324d93459

5. Bound `FileTime` read state (session/file map caps)
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/c055e6baa

6. Cap + throttle shell output streaming updates (`/session/.../shell` + bash tool)
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/e3fdd9a50

7. Docs for shell memory guardrails
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/476d693f1

8. Config/docs visibility for `snapshot: false` workaround
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/267433556

### Workarounds / options to reduce memory usage now

1. Disable workspace snapshots (can reduce memory + I/O in long sessions):
```json
{
  "snapshot": false
}
```

2. Keep MCP servers disabled unless needed (`mcp.<name>.enabled: false`), then enable selectively.

3. Prefer lower-output shell usage patterns (very large continuous stdout/stderr still creates pressure even with caps/throttling).

4. Keep compaction enabled (`compaction.auto: true`, `compaction.prune: true`).

### Important note

`snapshot: false` is a mitigation and can help significantly for some workloads, but it is not a full root-cause guarantee by itself. The larger stability improvement comes from combining it with the runtime fixes above (MCP fanout prevention + shell stream caps/throttling + reduced clone churn + bounded file-time state).

### Current status

After these changes, stress probes showed major RSS reduction on high-output shell scenarios versus pre-fix runs. Continuing to monitor long multi-session usage for remaining growth vectors (especially long-lived session/message retention patterns and LSP-heavy workloads).

1. `c673d81df` — serve memory workload profiler (+ threshold stop/docs consolidated)

5. `3035ace23` — remove deep clone churn on part update bus events

- `fix(bash): spool output to disk instead of in-memory capping`
- commit: https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode/commit/9b16b0c33

What changed:

3. In-memory state keeps only a bounded preview for metadata/UI updates.

This keeps memory bounded while preserving full command output for post-processing (Read/Grep) without clipping the underlying output stream.

### Update: DCP Plugin vs OpenCode Core Distinction

After further investigation, I want to clarify the distinction between two separate compression mechanisms:

| Feature | Source | Status |
|---------|--------|--------|
| `compress` tool | **DCP Plugin** (`@tarquinen/opencode-dcp`) | ✅ Works correctly |
| `/compact` command | **OpenCode Core** | ❌ Broken |

**Key Findings:**

1. The `compress` tool I have access to comes from the **Dynamic Context Pruning (DCP) plugin**, evidenced by:
   - System tags named `<dcp-message-id>` and `<dcp-system-reminder>`
   - The plugin `@tarquinen/opencode-dcp` is installed

2. The DCP plugin's `compress` tool **works correctly** - I successfully used it to compress earlier conversation ranges (confirmed by compressed block count increasing)

3. OpenCode's **built-in `/compact` command** is the broken one - it shows no TUI feedback and doesn't actually compress the context

**This means:**
- Users with the DCP plugin have a working agent-side compression mechanism
- Users without the DCP plugin have NO working compression at all
- The native `/compact` command needs to be fixed in OpenCode core

**Recommendation:**
The OpenCode team should investigate why the native `/compact` command doesn't trigger actual compression, while the DCP plugin's `compress` tool works as expected.

## Confirming — also affects Task tool (subagent dispatch), not just direct `opencode run`

**Environment:** opencode 1.2.26, macOS (darwin), GitHub Copilot provider

### Reproduction scenario

We run a discovery pipeline that uses `opencode run` in headless mode to launch a master orchestrator, which then dispatches ~15 sequential subagent Tasks via the Task tool. Each Task creates a child session that reads files, analyzes code, and writes draft reports.

```bash
# Master session (Sonnet 4.6) dispatches workers (GPT-5.4 per agent definition)
opencode run -m github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4.6 \
  "Read master-orchestrator.md and follow its instructions..."
```

### Observations across 3 independent batch runs tonight (8, 12, and 4 sessions)

| Run | Sessions | Model (master/worker) | Agents completed | Drafts written | Outcome |
|-----|----------|----------------------|------------------|---------------|---------|
| 1 | 8 | Sonnet 4.6 / GPT-5.4 | 2 of 120 | 0 | All stalled |
| 2 | 12 | Sonnet 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 | 0 of 180 | 0 | All stalled |
| 3 | 4 | Sonnet 4.6 / GPT-5.4 | 0 of 60 | 0 | All stalled |

One leftover GPT-5.4 session from run 1 did eventually produce 1 draft file before being killed, suggesting the bug is non-deterministic.

### Log evidence

The OpenCode internal log (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/`) confirms @alephmelo's finding:

1. Session initializes correctly (reads files, runs bash commands, dispatches first Task)
2. **Log output stops completely** at the moment the first subagent Task is dispatched
3. Log file shows 581 lines, all timestamped within the first 23 seconds — then absolute silence for 14+ minutes
4. Processes remain alive (confirmed via `ps`), consuming 500-900 MB RSS each, but at 0-2% CPU
5. No ERROR or WARN entries in the log — the hang is completely silent

### Additional data points

- **This pipeline produced 900+ drafts successfully before March 10** using the same agent definitions and headless invocation pattern
- The opencode binary was updated to v1.2.26 on March 13
- `github-copilot/gpt-5.4` workers are also affected (not just Sonnet)
- The `permission=task pattern=discovery-worker` evaluation shows `action: allow` — permissions are not the blocker

### Impact

The infinite agentic loop in headless mode breaks any automation that uses Task/subagent dispatch, since the parent session blocks on `<-done` (agent-tool.go:128) waiting for the child session to return. If the child enters the empty-loop state, the parent hangs forever, cascading upward.
